claims.text: Tungsten carbide catalysts can provide enhanced catalytic activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).
Tungsten carbide catalysts can provide enhanced catalytic activity for the hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR).
Tungsten carbide catalysts can provide enhanced durability during HER and HOR operation.
Tungsten carbide has a Pt-like electronic structure.
The Pt-like electronic structure of tungsten carbide enables nearly optimal hydrogen adsorption and binding.
Balanced hydrogen adsorption and desorption on tungsten carbide reduce the activation barrier for HER and HOR.
The robust carbide framework of tungsten carbide improves catalyst stability.
The structural robustness of tungsten carbide improves resistance to degradation during electrochemical cycling.
Nanostructured tungsten carbide can be synthesized by chemical vapor deposition.
Optimizing the microstructure and surface composition of tungsten carbide can increase the number or effectiveness of active sites.
Controlled annealing or doping can improve the stability of tungsten carbide catalysts.
Under identical acidic-electrolyte test conditions, tungsten carbide will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than pure Pt catalysts.
Under prolonged electrochemical cycling, tungsten carbide will degrade less than pure Pt catalysts.
Tungsten carbide catalyst performance is sensitive to synthesis and preparation parameters.
Particle-size distribution and surface modification can influence tungsten carbide catalyst performance.
Operational conditions and catalyst supports can affect the magnitude of the proposed performance improvement.
HER and HOR performance will be evaluated in acidic electrolyte using cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry.
A conventional Pt catalyst tested under identical conditions will serve as the experimental control.
